Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates software engineering agents on real GitHub issues by asking the model to produce a code patch that makes a project’s tests pass. The “Verified” subset consists of tasks filtered/validated to be solvable and to have reliable evaluation via reproducible test suites.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends the SWE-bench paradigm beyond Python to multiple programming languages, measuring whether an agent can understand repositories, diagnostics, and tests across different language ecosystems. It emphasizes cross-language generalization in realistic bug-fix and feature-fix workflows.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a larger and more challenging software engineering benchmark designed to be more contamination-resistant and industrially relevant, spanning multiple languages and harder real-world tasks. Models must produce correct patches under realistic repository constraints, often requiring deeper debugging and broader codebase understanding.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agentic performance in command-line environments where the model must execute multi-step tasks using shell commands, file edits, and program execution. It measures end-to-end autonomy under tool feedback, including diagnosing errors and iterating until the environment state satisfies the task goal.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Logical Reasoning, Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: BrowseComp evaluates “deep research” style browsing by requiring models to search, read, and synthesize information from a controlled set of web documents, emphasizing reproducibility over open-web variability. Success depends on finding the right sources, integrating evidence, and producing a grounded final answer.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Attention, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory, Decision-making (minor)
L3:

Description: τ2-bench measures interactive tool use in realistic customer-support-like scenarios (e.g., retail, airline, telecom) with multi-turn dialogue, policy constraints, and API calls. Agents must coordinate conversation with a simulated user while using tools correctly and adhering to domain policies.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor), Language Production (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control

Description: OSWorld evaluates multimodal computer-use agents operating a desktop-like environment, requiring navigation of GUIs, reading screens, and executing actions (click, type, open apps) to complete tasks. It stresses long-horizon interaction grounded in visual state, with tool feedback and error recovery.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Visual Attention & Eye Movements (minor), Sensorimotor Coordination (minor)
L3:

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a fluid reasoning benchmark of abstract grid transformation problems where models infer hidden rules from a few input–output examples and apply them to new inputs. It is designed to reduce reliance on memorized knowledge and instead emphasize novel pattern induction and compositional reasoning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Planning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon autonomous agency in a simulated business setting where an agent manages a vending-machine operation over extended time, making thousands of decisions. Performance is typically measured by final profit/balance and requires coherent strategy, adaptation, and sustained goal pursuit.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Reward Mechanisms
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor), Self-reflection (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas evaluates real-world tool use through the Model Context Protocol by testing whether models can discover tools, invoke them correctly, and complete multi-step workflows across MCP servers. Tasks emphasize tool selection, parameterization, error handling, and synthesis of tool outputs into correct responses.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: FinanceAgent measures whether models can perform entry-level financial analyst tasks, such as interpreting financial documents, performing calculations, building analyses, and producing professional outputs. It stresses domain knowledge, quantitative reasoning, and structured reporting aligned to task constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory, Planning (minor), Decision-making (minor)
L3:

Description: CyberGym evaluates cybersecurity agent capabilities on real-world vulnerability tasks, including identifying known vulnerabilities from descriptions and, in some settings, discovering new issues. It typically requires code reading, hypothesis testing, and iterating with tool feedback to validate findings.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Attention (minor), Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SpreadsheetBench evaluates spreadsheet manipulation and analysis by giving models realistic spreadsheet tasks that require reading, editing, computing, and formatting structured tabular data. Agent harnesses often involve tool use (e.g., Python or office libraries) to update files and verify outputs.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Working Memory, Logical Reasoning, Decision-making (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: Humanity’s Last Exam is a difficult multimodal benchmark intended to probe frontier knowledge and reasoning across many domains with challenging questions. It is often evaluated both with and without tools (e.g., search/code), emphasizing synthesis, correctness, and robustness under uncertainty.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory, Multisensory Integration (minor), Planning (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: AIME 2025 evaluates competition-style mathematics problem solving from the American Invitational Mathematics Examination. Tasks require multi-step derivations, careful algebraic/number-theoretic reasoning, and high precision in final answers.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GPQA Diamond is a high-quality subset of the GPQA benchmark with extremely challenging graduate-level science multiple-choice questions that are difficult to answer via superficial pattern matching. It emphasizes deep domain understanding and multi-step scientific reasoning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: MMMLU extends MMLU to multiple languages, testing broad academic knowledge and reasoning across many subjects in non-English settings. It measures multilingual generalization, including whether a model can maintain consistent competence across languages and domains.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension, Language Production (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMU is a multimodal benchmark spanning many disciplines where models answer questions that require integrating images (diagrams, charts, photos) with text. It probes visual understanding, cross-domain reasoning, and the ability to ground answers in visual evidence.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Multisensory Integration, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMU-Pro is a harder, more “professional-grade” variant of MMMU intended to better separate top multimodal models, often with more complex questions and evaluation design. It emphasizes reliable visual grounding and higher-level reasoning over multimodal inputs.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Multisensory Integration, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: LAB-Bench FigQA evaluates whether models can correctly interpret scientific figures from biology papers and answer questions that depend on reading plots, panels, labels, and experimental context. It targets research-relevant visual reasoning rather than generic image captioning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: WebArena evaluates autonomous web agents that must complete tasks on realistic web apps (e-commerce, forums, CMS, etc.) through multi-step navigation and interaction. It measures grounded decision-making over dynamic interfaces, including robustness to partial observability and long action sequences.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Working Memory, Visual Attention & Eye Movements (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: MathArena Apex aggregates very difficult math problems (often at or beyond contest level) and reports model performance under standardized conditions. It emphasizes sustained multi-step reasoning and accuracy across diverse advanced topics.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: ScreenShot-Pro evaluates understanding of high-resolution GUI screenshots by asking models to answer questions or take actions grounded in interface elements and layout. It targets practical visual grounding in software UIs, where small text, icons, and spatial relationships matter.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Attention, Working Memory (minor), Visual Attention & Eye Movements (minor)
L3:

Description: CharXiv Reasoning evaluates models on questions that require interpreting scientific charts/figures (often from research papers) and performing structured reasoning over plotted data. It emphasizes extracting quantitative relationships and drawing correct conclusions from visual evidence.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: OmniDocBench 1.5 evaluates document understanding and OCR across heterogeneous content such as text, formulas, tables, and reading order. It measures whether models can accurately parse complex layouts and reproduce content with low edit distance against ground truth.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception, Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Attention, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: Video-MMMU extends multimodal understanding to video, requiring models to integrate information over time (multiple frames/clips) and answer questions that depend on events, actions, and temporal context. It probes robust video reasoning beyond single-image cues.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Multisensory Integration, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Working Memory, Attention (minor)
L3: Cognitive Timing & Predictive Modeling (minor)

Description: LiveCodeBench Pro evaluates code generation and problem solving on programming tasks, often designed to reflect modern competitive programming and practical coding scenarios. It focuses on correctness under strict tests and is commonly summarized with an Elo-style rating for head-to-head performance.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning, Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3:

Description: FACTS Benchmark Suite evaluates factuality and grounding behaviors across a collection of tests designed to measure when models make unsupported claims or hallucinate. It emphasizes calibration, citation/grounding behavior (when applicable), and correctness under diverse factual prompts.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control, Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SimpleQA Verified evaluates short-form question answering with an emphasis on verified correctness and reduced ambiguity, typically using strict grading. It is intended to measure whether models can provide precise factual answers without drifting into plausible-sounding but incorrect responses.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Inhibitory Control, Self-reflection (minor)

Description: Global PIQA is a multilingual/non-parallel variant of physical commonsense reasoning QA, where models choose or generate answers about everyday interactions with objects and environments across languages. It probes whether “intuitive physics” and procedural commonsense generalize beyond English.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MRCR v2 (8-needle) evaluates long-context multi-round coreference and retrieval: multiple similar “needle” requests are embedded in long transcripts, and the model must reproduce the response associated with a specified needle. The 8-needle setting increases interference and tests robust information access over long contexts.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Working Memory, Attention, Episodic Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GDPval evaluates economically valuable, well-specified knowledge-work tasks across many occupations, with expert judges comparing model outputs to professional baselines. Tasks often require producing real work artifacts (e.g., spreadsheets, presentations, plans) under explicit constraints and quality standards.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SWE-Lancer evaluates software engineering capability on repository-based tasks that resemble real development work, including implementing changes and fixing issues within larger codebases. It is intended to reflect practical engineering impact beyond small standalone coding puzzles.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Decision-making (minor), Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3:

Description: Graphwalks evaluates reasoning over graph-structured data, such as following edges, performing traversals (e.g., BFS-like tasks), and answering questions about nodes reachable under constraints. It stresses precise multi-step relational reasoning and resistance to distraction from near-miss paths.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Attention, Spatial Representation & Mapping
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Toolathon evaluates how reliably models can use external tools across diverse tool-use tasks, including selecting the right tool, forming correct calls, and composing multi-step tool workflows. It emphasizes robustness to tool errors, state tracking across turns, and correct final synthesis.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor), Self-reflection (minor)

Description: HMMT evaluates contest mathematics performance using problems associated with the Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. It emphasizes deep multi-step problem solving, careful case analysis, and precision under competition-style constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: FrontierMath evaluates expert-level mathematics, including very challenging problems intended to be difficult for both humans and models, often reported by difficulty tiers. It emphasizes sustained reasoning, rigorous derivations, and (when tools are allowed) correct integration of computation with proof-like logic.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor), Self-reflection (minor)
